title: Sorting and grouping: change presentation while preserving requests
goal: Order requests by duration, group them by customer and distinguish presentation from data edits and report totals.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 2; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: From a familiar situation to a checkable question
paragraphs: A 45-minute request was at the top; after a click 15 is there. Did the request change? Sorting changes order, grouping adds context, and a report calculates a total. Track four numbers so similar screens do not blur these operations.

sections.title: Where to act
paragraphs: Work in the installed training service. Nexus stores the lesson and your note, but does not change the external infobase. Give report control its own separate practice with the four specified requests; 0/1440 probes and earlier 20/55 must not silently enter its total. Preserve earlier infobases. The ready-made report requires no BSL.

sections.title: Sorting changes row order
paragraphs: Clicking the numeric column header changes list order; another click switches direction. Check actual values rather than guessing a small arrow’s meaning. For 30, 45, 30 and 15, ascending order is 15, 30, 30, 45; descending is 45, 30, 30, 15.

Document numbers and fields do not change. The second row after sorting may be a different request. Identify your document by its actual number. Equal durations do not guarantee a particular relative order without an additional sort criterion.

sections.title: Reason before acting
paragraphs: Two documents can share duration 30 without being duplicates.
Identify the infobase, list and particular record separately. A command, visible text and saved state are different things.

code.source:

Ascending: 15, 30, 30, 45.
Descending: 45, 30, 30, 15.
By customer: three documents and one.

tables.caption: A collapsed group still retains data

sections.title: Grouping puts related details under a heading
paragraphs: Grouping by Клиент places requests linked to the same customer under one heading. This uses a customer reference rather than similar text. Two same-named customer records can form different groups; investigate identity before changing names for cosmetic consistency.
A plus beside a group expands its details. A collapsed group does not imply missing or deleted documents. Its heading is not an additional request: count document numbers rather than visible bands.

sections.title: Predict the result
paragraphs: Must the two 30-minute requests exchange places in ascending order?

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. Equal values do not define their relative order when sorting by a single field. Add actual number as a second key for a reproducible order. Check preservation by the four numbers and their fields, not row positions.

sections.title: Keep one dataset for subsequent lessons
paragraphs: The sequential route already has 30, 45 and 30 minutes for the first customer, including the corrected request from the preceding lesson. Add one separate 15-minute request for the existing second customer Учебный Юг, using the existing service. Preserve earlier records.

If you already created that request, reuse its number instead of duplicating it. The basic example has three first-customer requests and one second-customer request. Preserve additional work and recalculate expected groups from your actual table.

sections.title: Context and transitions
paragraphs: Read the path and explain what changes at each step. The diagram does not operate the external application.

flow.caption: Explore the example: One dataset, several presentations
alternative: Groups: First: 3; second: 1 → Details remain available.

sections.title: Check the explanation’s boundary
paragraphs: Do not delete equal durations as duplicates or mistake a collapsed group for lost data.
Identify your request by actual number rather than its former position.

sections.title: Order, group and aggregate are different
paragraphs: Sorting chooses order, grouping organizes related details and filtering chooses which rows are included. They can act together. Disable your duration filter before sorting, otherwise excluded values remain hidden. Grouped presentation can also affect where a sort is applied.

A normal list grouping does not promise an automatic duration total in the heading. The next lesson’s separate report calculates count and minutes as aggregates. Here reconcile numbers and manually calculate 105 minutes for the first customer and 15 for the second.

sections.title: A new independent task
paragraphs: Use your separate East 20/55/40, West 45 set from the previous topic. Predict ascending and descending minute order. Configure sorting, then grouping by customer. Find every one of the four numbers; explain how grouping differs from a report total. Remove the settings and verify that request values did not change.
Record a prediction first. After your own attempt reveal the reference and compare the selected record as well as its number.

selfcheck.prompt: Must the two 30-minute requests exchange places in ascending order?
options: No: equal keys do not define order
selfcheck.feedback: No. Equal values do not define their relative order when sorting by a single field. Add actual number as a second key for a reproducible order. Check preservation by the four numbers and their fields, not row positions.

selfcheck.prompt: What does a plus sign beside a group mean?
Two documents have 30 minutes. What distinguishes their identity?
selfcheck.feedback: An equal field value does not establish one record.

selfcheck.prompt: East’s group contains three details. Are these three customers?
options: No: three requests for one customer
Yes: every row is a new customer
No: only one request is saved
selfcheck.feedback: Ascending reads 20, 40, 45, 55; descending 55, 45, 40, 20. East has three detail records; West one. A group heading is not a new request, and a collapsed detail row is not deleted. A report separately gives East 3/115, West 1/45, total 4/160; sorting alone does not add that calculation. Removing settings preserves all fields at the previous numbers. Distinguish my UI experiment from the author’s query-order check.
